sources.role: canonical raw-grade identities and backward-compatible grade migration
daily external mine supply, operating inventory and persistent configuration
editable daily grade arrivals and transactional persistence
built-in scenario data and train-export specifications
shared MPH blend catalogue, campaign state, quality and receiving reachability
optional variable-throughput blend construction, physical readiness and used-receiver quality
protected objective passes and minimum job volume
stockpile-enabled site-level pre-washing matrix catalogues, optimized shares and validation
atomic scenario-keyed blending enablement persistence without physical-state changes
closed-loop execution and hard quality holds

parameters.name: Daily mine arrivals
parameters.meaning: Prescribed external raw-grade supply by site/civil day, converted to conserved whole-tonne bucket inflows at existing finite buffers; obsolete RAW-BT-NOMINAL records are mass-preservingly folded into RAW-BT; optional operating versus legacy exact closing stock policy.
parameters.basis: as-handled wet mass, civil days and absolute bucket offsets
parameters.notes: Default volume/mix are assumptions, not measurements. Custom terminal commitments and WIP closure survive. Execution distinguishes scheduled, accepted and rejected arrivals. Prewash shares remain source-pile, not individual grade, shares.

parameters.name: Objective mode
parameters.meaning: Selects protected service-first refinement or one weighted sum.

parameters.name: Minimum complete job volume
parameters.meaning: Hard mass floor on a complete contiguous job; zero disables it.

parameters.name: Qualified-service degradation allowance
parameters.meaning: Maximum deterioration allowed when protecting primary qualified service during refinement.

parameters.name: Washing dry-solids yield
parameters.meaning: Fraction of feed dry solids retained in product for washing option k; defaults are 0.85 for Simple and 0.65 for Full.

parameters.name: Washing characteristic change
parameters.meaning: Relative percentage change applied to each known feed characteristic. Default vectors [BPL,Cd,MgO,SiO2,CO2,moisture] are [+12,-5,-30,-28,-26,+20]% for Simple and [+23,-20,-64,-50,-27,+20]% for Full.

parameters.name: Washing treatment unit cost
parameters.meaning: Cost per product dry-solids tonne for washing option k.

parameters.name: Provisional G10 receiving limits
parameters.meaning: Hard assay intervals applied to the permanent G10 demand contract at configured PAP receiving destinations.

parameters.name: RAW-TBT planning assay
parameters.meaning: Configured raw-TBT vector BPL 54.10%, Cd 16 ppm, MgO 1.52%, SiO2 14.39%, CO2 8.32%, and retained prior moisture 12%; the separately supplied 5% H2O value is explicitly excluded.

parameters.name: Pre-washing feed blend policy
parameters.meaning: Version 4 selects one shared mode and reusable matrix catalogue or optimized envelope per site, with enabled_source_spaces switches per stockpile applying across physical washing stages. A disabled required input excludes a whole matrix without renormalization. Insufficient/infeasible enabled sources leave blending inactive while ordinary washing remains available. Legacy points without the new source key retain line scoping.
parameters.basis: blend point, washing stage and civil day

parameters.name: Shared MPH humid-stockpile blend policy
parameters.meaning: Version 7 defines one global blend mode, reusable matrix catalogue or optimized share envelope, and a 500 t adjustable minimum per selected input grade. A pile enable flag permits optional construction, with variable quantity and resulting grade, calculated completion time and derived passes. Legacy v5/v6 policies retain their fixed campaign contract.

parameters.name: Minimum contribution per used blend input grade
parameters.meaning: Default 500 physical tonnes, adjustable globally; aggregate input-grade tonnes per constructed pile, not a minimum per job or time bucket. Integer scheduling uses max(ceil(L),1) when a grade is selected.
parameters.basis: selected input grade and pile construction

variables.name: Demand-driven pile activity and composition
variables.symbol: A[h], Q[h], q[h,g], U[h,g], Z[h,k], Ready[h,t]
variables.meaning: Optional pile construction selects a variable physical total and at least two input grades, each meeting the absolute floor. Fixed-matrix ratios scale exactly with total or optimized shares follow common bounds. Readiness becomes true at the first boundary at which all selected tonnes were stacked.
variables.basis: enabled stockpile, input grade, catalogue entry and boundary
variables.domain: nonnegative integer tonnes and binary indicators

variables.name: Candidate input flow
variables.meaning: Selected physical/as-handled input mass for candidate c in bucket t.

variables.name: Activity group state
variables.meaning: One when an activity group owns its machine in a bucket.

variables.name: Physical inventory
variables.meaning: Physical mass present at a stock/process space boundary.

variables.name: Material-pool inventory
variables.meaning: Grade-resolved mass under the physical inventory total when washing is enabled.
variables.basis: space, material pool and bucket boundary

variables.name: Unmet demand
variables.meaning: Explicit shortage slack in the demand balance.
variables.basis: destination due bucket or process-feed campaign

variables.name: Soft quality slack
variables.meaning: Violation of a soft delivered-quality limit after model scaling.

variables.name: Safety-stock shortfall
variables.meaning: Positive deficit below configured safety stock.

variables.name: Continuous-feed gap
variables.meaning: One when delivery is below the configured service threshold in a demand-active bucket.

variables.name: Machine transition and hold state
variables.meaning: Exact bucket transition events and running-without-flow state.

variables.name: Below-floor parcel exception
variables.meaning: One when an active bucket moves less than its configured parcel floor and pays a penalty.

objective_terms.name: Emergency slack
objective_terms.meaning: Spill, unstacked/surge slack, and process-stage target shortfall.

objective_terms.name: Qualified service shortfall
objective_terms.meaning: Priority-weighted demand not served by material credited as quality-qualified.

objective_terms.name: Unqualified dispatch
objective_terms.meaning: Delivered mass that does not reduce quality-qualified shortage.

objective_terms.name: Raw washing-feed dry mass
objective_terms.meaning: Dry mass sent to washing; minimizing it favors higher recovery for a protected product requirement.

objective_terms.name: Washing treatment cost
objective_terms.meaning: Nominal recovered-dry-product treatment-cost proxy expressed through input flow and a rounded per-input-tonne coefficient.
objective_terms.basis: nominal washing product dry mass before integer output rounding
objective_terms.formula: sum X_wet_t * round(1000 * cost_per_tsm_t * input_dry_fraction * nominal_dry_yield) / 1000
objective_terms.notes: Nominal-yield objective proxy precedes whole-tonne output rounding; distinguish from cost computed on serialized physical product flows.

objective_terms.name: Continuous-feed interruptions
objective_terms.meaning: Penalty on gap minutes and new interruption episodes.

objective_terms.name: Equipment operating events
objective_terms.meaning: Penalty on starts, stops, group changeovers, and held buckets.

objective_terms.name: Remaining planning preferences
objective_terms.meaning: Protected last-tier aggregate of remaining weighted and tie-breaker terms.

objective_terms.name: Weighted unmet demand
objective_terms.meaning: Priority-weighted unmet demand contribution in the legacy weighted objective.

objective_terms.name: Weighted quality violation
objective_terms.meaning: Soft destination and blend quality slack contribution.

constraints.name: Candidate eligibility and reachability
constraints.meaning: Only validated routes, machines, materials, lifecycle states, and known required assays become candidates.

constraints.name: Flow, activity and machine-rate linkage
constraints.meaning: Active candidates respect per-bucket feasible rate bounds; inactive candidates move zero.

constraints.name: Machine exclusivity, calendars and fixed jobs
constraints.meaning: A machine has at most one activity group per bucket and respects availability and fixed assignments.

constraints.name: Link/shared/conflict capacity
constraints.meaning: Candidate flow respects link capacities, shared envelopes, corridor confluence, and conflict groups.

constraints.name: Physical inventory balance
constraints.meaning: Closing inventory equals opening inventory plus inflows minus outflows and loss/spill terms.

constraints.name: Grade-resolved material balance
constraints.meaning: Material-pool inventories conserve reachable material and sum to physical inventory.

constraints.name: Demand balance with unmet slack
constraints.meaning: Credited delivered mass plus explicit unmet mass equals requested mass on the applicable due basis.
constraints.basis: destination bucket or daily process campaign

constraints.name: Mass-weighted quality limits
constraints.meaning: Delivered blends satisfy hard limits; soft limits may use penalized quality slack. Version 7 pile chemistry is qualified against each destination/specification profile actually supplied, using selected component assays. Legacy fixed campaigns retain reachable-receiver checks even in a zero-demand construction window.

constraints.name: Campaign-selected receiving specification
constraints.meaning: A demand specification grade selects its receiving envelope by bucket without requiring the physical source-grade label to match; quality windows split at contract changes and unknown required assays are excluded.
constraints.basis: destination, demand campaign and quality window
constraints.hardness: hard or soft by selected specification

constraints.name: Permanent PAP G10 demand contract
constraints.meaning: PAP-1 and PAP-2 destination defaults and every explicit demand bucket request G10; presets and the washing-treatment toggle cannot replace it with a physical stream grade.
constraints.hardness: hard pre-solve contract plus hard G10 assay limits

constraints.name: Washing quality and yield conversion
constraints.meaning: Output assays use relative changes and wet output follows dry-solids yield and moisture conversion.

constraints.name: Daily pre-washing source-share and mode constraints
constraints.meaning: For every effective physical washing stage and civil day, MATRIX selects at most one eligible recipe whose positive source inputs are enabled and enforces its exact percentages; OPTIMIZED uses only enabled source bounds. All nonzero blend-participating feed uses one common allowed washing mode; ordinary nonblend feed is separate.
constraints.basis: blend point, washing stage and civil day

constraints.name: MPH shared matrix catalogue selection
constraints.meaning: For each active unresolved v7 M16 construction in MATRIX mode, one shared catalogue recipe is selected and its rational percentages scale with the chosen total whole tonnes. Enabled piles may remain inactive. No recipe is a permanent pile assignment; legacy fixed campaigns retain their configured total allocation.
constraints.basis: enabled M16 pile campaign and catalogue matrix

constraints.name: Blend completion and reclaim gate
constraints.meaning: A new v7 construction has no configured deadline. Reclaim requires complete selected component tonnes. Execution freezes the exact recipe/quantity and verifies lot identity; a planned timestamp alone cannot release it. A completed/depleted empty pile may reopen for a later lot, while prior job accounting remains preserved across snapshots and actual shortfalls hold the next lot.

constraints.name: Continuous-feed gap policy
constraints.meaning: Defines gap state from minimum service threshold and can enforce a configured hard maximum gap.

constraints.name: Safety-stock target
constraints.meaning: Inventory below safety stock creates an integrated penalized shortfall.

constraints.name: Minimum complete contiguous job volume
constraints.meaning: If enabled, every completed contiguous job must accumulate at least the configured mass.

constraints.name: Minute execution acceptance
constraints.meaning: A candidate solution is accepted only when its minute placement and physical validation contracts pass.

algorithms.name: Planning strategy routing
algorithms.meaning: Validates global model state and selects the mixed-resolution, weekly rolling, or uniform execution strategy.
steps: route by resolution and horizon flags
algorithms.termination: Returns explicit ERROR for invalid input or the selected strategy's result.

algorithms.name: Uniform-grid CP-SAT solve
algorithms.meaning: Builds and solves one complete CP-SAT model, validates minute execution, applies protected refinements, and extracts the accepted result.
steps: if the physical washing seed is absent, attempt bounded feasibility on an unrestricted clone of the original hard typed model
algorithms.termination: Returns OPTIMAL or FEASIBLE only with an accepted incumbent; a rejected executable candidate can be PARTIAL, while absent incumbents return INFEASIBLE, UNKNOWN, or ERROR. PARTIAL is not a usable replacement plan.

algorithms.name: Quality-aware physical washing seed
algorithms.meaning: First verifies a no-command incumbent against the unchanged hard model, then attempts a richer typed washing/dispatch hint while preferring the highest-yield treatment that individually satisfies G10. The mapper replays grade-specific exogenous flows at the authoritative bucket boundary and retains legitimate bounded external overflow. Typed-only PAP certification and chevron construction remain authoritative in the full model.
algorithms.basis: one uniform planning window with washing enabled
inputs: prepared material pools and candidate variants
typed exogenous-flow material map and explicit slack/overflow contracts
outputs: candidate flow seed or explicit unmapped diagnostic
steps: verify a no-command incumbent on a clone of the complete hard model
zero PAP demand and disable chevron construction only on the label-only precursor copy
identify treatment variants whose transformed assays satisfy G10
select the highest-yield qualifying mode or highest-yield fallback and apply the conservative capacity/yield envelope across reachable materials
replay typed exogenous flows after commanded bucket work and allocate bounded external overflow
map available opening pools to managed dispatches
clamp satisfied dispatch requirements at zero
use inconsistent mapped restrictions only as repairable hints or retain the verified emergency incumbent
algorithms.termination: Every richer seed is advisory and bounded. The authoritative objective search may alter all decisions. If that search times out, the same-hard-model emergency incumbent may be returned as FEASIBLE with all unmet demand, target shortfall and overflow visible; this is not a service-quality or optimality certificate.

algorithms.name: Protected lexicographic refinement
algorithms.meaning: Optimizes secondary levels sequentially while constraining every previously accepted level to its permitted ceiling.
steps: solve each level within remaining budgets
algorithms.termination: A failed, timed-out, or rejected level retains the previous accepted incumbent; later levels cannot degrade protected ceilings.

algorithms.name: State-coupled weekly rolling solve
algorithms.meaning: Partitions a long horizon into civil-day windows, solves them sequentially, carries physical and operational state, and merges the results.
outputs: merged weekly PlanResult or explicit partial/failed result
steps: coalesce unresolved legacy fixed-deadline blend lookahead; v7 has no preset readiness boundary
carry inventory, delayed material, belt, machine and feed-gap state, plus exact selected blend composition, total, matrix, label and calculated completion
algorithms.termination: Stops on first non-usable window or exhausted total wall budget; optimality is not a monolithic whole-week certificate.

algorithms.name: Tactical plus fine-prefix solve
algorithms.meaning: Solves a complete tactical plan, resamples and re-optimizes its near-term prefix, then merges the accepted prefix with the tactical tail.
outputs: merged mixed-resolution result or feasible tactical fallback
algorithms.termination: Tactical failure is returned; resample, wall, or fine-prefix failure after a feasible tactical solve retains a labelled tactical fallback.

algorithms.name: Minute-execution acceptance and repair
algorithms.meaning: Tests whether bucket decisions can be placed into valid minute execution windows and adds incompatibility cuts when repair is needed.
outputs: accepted execution windows or repair constraints
steps: accept valid incumbent or add cuts
algorithms.termination: Only validated execution is accepted; failure of a later repair attempt retains a previously accepted incumbent where one exists.

algorithms.name: Protected parcel consolidation
algorithms.meaning: Optionally reduces short command buckets while fixing selected mass, service, inventory, slack, and protected objective quantities.
algorithms.basis: feasible primary plan with short parcels
outputs: accepted consolidated incumbent or unchanged primary incumbent
algorithms.termination: Any exception, rejection, or non-improvement leaves the valid primary incumbent unchanged.

kpis.name: Derived chevron equivalent traversals
kpis.meaning: Display estimate of one-way stacking traversals from validated flow duration, or scheduled tonnes divided by flow rate, multiplied by explicitly configured stacking traverse speed and divided by supported pile/work-area length. The displayed integer rounds upward; missing physical inputs leave the estimate unavailable.

kpis.name: Demand service
kpis.meaning: Credited delivered mass divided by requested demand over the evaluated horizon.
kpis.basis: due bucket; daily grade campaign for process-feed

kpis.name: Final-product service
kpis.meaning: On-time final-product delivery divided by final-product demand, excluding process-feed campaigns.

kpis.name: On-spec delivered observations
kpis.meaning: Share of positive-delivery destination/bucket observations satisfying every configured quality limit.

kpis.name: On-spec evaluated final-product mass
kpis.meaning: On-spec final-product delivered mass divided by quality-evaluated final-product delivered mass.

kpis.name: Actual washing dry yield
kpis.meaning: Product dry mass divided by feed dry mass for one treatment mode.

kpis.name: Washing treatment cost
kpis.meaning: Planned KPI copies the coefficient-rounded nominal-yield objective proxy. Simulated KPI recomputes recovered physical product dry mass times option cost. These bases can differ after integer output rounding.
kpis.formula: planned: washing-treatment-cost objective proxy; simulated: sum actual_product_dry_t*cost_per_tsm_t

kpis.name: Integrated safety-stock shortfall
kpis.meaning: Time integral of positive safety-stock deficit.

kpis.name: Machine utilisation
kpis.meaning: Share of evaluated native buckets in which a machine is active.

kpis.name: Average route utilisation
kpis.meaning: Average transported rate divided by route capacity.

kpis.name: Schedule transition reconciliation residual
kpis.meaning: Unexplained difference between bucket-state and executed-minute transition identities; must be zero.

code_mappings.name: Demand-driven MPH blending
code_mappings.meaning: Constructs optional variable-volume pile blends, activates quality gates for used receiving profiles, and carries exact proposals into measured completion gates.

code_mappings.name: CP-SAT model construction
code_mappings.meaning: Candidate generation, variables, constraints, objectives, solve and extraction.

code_mappings.name: Protected objective refinement
code_mappings.meaning: Sequential secondary solves with explicit incumbent ceilings.

code_mappings.name: Washing material and quality model
code_mappings.meaning: Settings, transformations, G10 synchronization, and material expansion.

code_mappings.name: Pre-washing feed blending model
code_mappings.meaning: Validates physical source-to-line mappings and source-stockpile switches, filters eligible matrices or bounds, gates alternate feed routes, and constructs daily source-share/common-treatment-mode constraints only for active blend policies.

code_mappings.name: Quality-aware washing seed selection
code_mappings.meaning: Verifies a same-hard-model emergency incumbent, maps grade-typed exogenous arrivals and conservative multi-material treatment limits in the richer seed, selects a G10-capable treatment before yield tie-breaking, and never treats a failed advisory mapping as proof of full-model infeasibility.

code_mappings.name: Campaign receiving-specification mapping
code_mappings.meaning: Resolves demand-grade contracts into optimizer, execution and KPI quality semantics while preserving physical source identity.

code_mappings.name: Minute execution and physical runs
code_mappings.meaning: Transforms bucket allocations into validated execution windows and run identities.

code_mappings.name: KPI computation
code_mappings.meaning: Calculates planned or executed performance on the evaluated horizon.

code_mappings.name: Run evidence bundle
code_mappings.meaning: Normalizes exact inputs, decisions, state, outputs, KPIs and model context for analysis.

limitations.meaning: The verified no-command washing fallback is a feasibility guarantee only. It retains explicit unmet demand, planning-target shortfall and bounded external overflow and can therefore be operationally poor. FEASIBLE with this bootstrap reason does not establish adequate service, calibrated mine supply, or optimality.

The current uniform v7 solve supports one new construction lot per enabled pile; physical composition and selected total freeze on first actual stacking. An enabled completed/depleted pile with zero physical inventory can reopen at a later solve boundary and execute a subsequent lot. Incomplete blends cannot be reclaimed or treated as selective constituent pools. Rolling windows optimize locally, without a configured batch or readiness deadline; no whole-week optimality or detailed spatial homogenization is implied.

Chevron equivalent passes are derived display metadata from validated flow duration (or tonnes/rate), explicit stacking traverse speed and configured geometry. Missing inputs leave the count unavailable. Repositioning speed is not used as stacking speed; this calculation is not a layer-by-layer stockpile model or plant validation.

Pre-washing represents daily feed shares through explicit common reclaim routes, not spatial stockpile-face homogenization. Sites support shared matrices or optimized envelopes and per-source-stockpile enablement. Default all-source enablement, optimized 5-95% bounds and both treatment modes are commissioning assumptions. Treated component pools remain selectively reclaimable downstream; G10 receipt chemistry need not match the complete daily campaign. Legacy imported points without source switches retain earlier line-scoped policies.

RAW-TBT chemistry and the G10 profile were supplied by the project team but are not independently approved here. Washing yields and quality changes remain a provisional behavior calibration. TBT-to-Full and low-Cd-to-Simple selectivity is code-verified, but the numeric process response is not plant validated.
Treatment cost excludes unmodelled transport, energy, water, reagents, disposal and capital effects.
Material pools do not predict reclaim-face geometry or stockpile layer progression.
Generated candidate evidence does not prove force-feasibility of an unused alternative.
Evidence-bundle residuals are not a complete dump of all internal CP-SAT constraints.

The source table's strict '<' limits are preserved in provenance but the current SpecRange contract implements inclusive numeric maxima; BG11 and BG AD also require distinct assays that current stock vectors may not provide.
